title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to the African Governance, Peace & Security Architectures

description.narrative: Contract related to: Support to the African Governance, Peace & Security Architectures - This Action seeks to contribute to the above joint principles as well as the African Union¿s (AU) Agenda 2063 and the ¿Silencing the Guns¿ flagship initiative (2020-2030). The latter¿s objective is to end all wars, civil conflicts, gender-based violence and violent conflicts, and prevent genocide by supporting: i) the APSA as the main framework for promoting peace, security and stability in Africa, and ii) the AGA in responding to the AU vision to promote and protect human and people¿s rights, consolidate democratic institutions, good governance and the rule of law on the continent. In addition, the Action further contributes to SDG 5: Gender Equality; SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions; and SDG 17: Partnership for the Goals. Specifically, this Action will support the African Governance Architecture (AGA) and African Peace and Security Architecture (APSA) to help prevent conflict and enhance participatory democratic governance across the African continent. This will be done by engaging with the AU Commission (AUC) and its continental organs, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and AU Member States (AUMS) at political, policy and operational levels. It represents a more focused support to the AU Governance, Peace and Security (GPS) Architectures, while continuing the EU¿s political commitment to the continent in the spirit of shared African-European priorities.Indeed, this Action proposes to gather formerly separate support programmes to APSA (peace and security) and AGA (governance)[1] under one conceptual roof by building on lesson learnt and wider consultations with the AU at various levels. With a planned budget of EUR 40 million over four years managed by the EUD to the AU, it will address key thematic issues of mutual interest and reinforce the GPS nexus. The Action responds to ongoing major AU reforms, notably i) the effective transformation of the Political Affairs, Peace, and Security Department (AU-PAPS) towards more integrated approaches to conflicts and their political root causes by addressing the Governance, Peace and Security (GPS) nexus; ii) the operationalisation of the AU Peace Fund; and iii) the rationalisation of the AU treaty-based human rights organs. Engagement with Pan-African civil society networks (CSOs), think tanks and academia is mainstreamed to build on positive results of previous programmes. To ensure the sustainability of GPS efforts, the need to engage with youth and women is widely recognised as instrumental to maximising the demographic dividend.
